Hero.title: Hisho (飛翔)
Hero.tagline: Next-generation trading software built for the Japanese stock market.

About.title: Our Mission
About.description: We are developing an innovative trading platform tailored specifically for Japan's stock market. Our goal is to provide an intuitive, high-speed, and reliable trading environment to help investors soar.

Rules.title: Exam Rules & Consent
Rules.rule1: This exam has a strict time limit of exactly 80 minutes, starting the moment you click 'Start.'
Rules.rule2: AI tools are strictly forbidden. Copy and paste is disabled throughout the exam.
Rules.rule3: Passing the coding section alone is not enough — candidates are evaluated on their answers across every section, so you should put effort into all parts, not just the coding questions.
Rules.rule4: If selected, the position is a paid 2-month internship at a salary of ¥80,000.
Rules.rule5: If our AI-detection process finds evidence that AI was used, the candidate will be blacklisted from this exam AND from any future position at the company.
Rules.checkbox: I have read and understood the rules above.

AntiCheat.warning: Copy/paste is disabled during this exam.

Exam.completedMessage: Your exam has been successfully submitted. Thank you for your time.

questions.q1: How familiar are you with the trading hours, rules, and general landscape of the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE)?
questions.q2: What do you see as the biggest cultural or economic barrier for everyday people in Japan looking to start investing in stocks?
questions.q3: How would you explain the difference between a "limit order" and a "market order" to a user who has never traded before?
questions.q4: If the Japanese government introduces a new regulation affecting day-trading margins, how would you ensure our company adapts its strategy quickly?
questions.q5: Why do you believe a localized trading platform is necessary for Japan, rather than just translating an international app like Robinhood or E-Trade?
questions.q6: Building a high-stakes financial platform is stressful. How do you manage your own stress and keep your team focused during critical times, like a major product launch?
questions.q7: What do you believe is the single most important soft skill a team member can have when working in the fintech industry?
questions.q8: Describe a time you noticed a company process that was inefficient or broken. How did you go about improving it?
questions.q9: If the marketing team wants to push an aggressive advertising campaign that you feel slightly misrepresents the platform's actual capabilities, how do you handle that internal conflict?
questions.q10: If a major competitor in the Japanese market launches a highly requested feature before we do, how should our company react?
questions.q11: Why are you specifically interested in joining a company focused on the Japanese stock market, rather than a generic tech or e-commerce startup?
questions.q12: What ethical considerations arise if we introduce social trading features (such as allowing users to view or copy popular portfolios)?
questions.q13: If platform analytics show a user has put 100% of their life savings into a single, highly volatile stock, should our platform intervene with a diversification warning, or remain a completely neutral execution tool? Why?
questions.q14: How would you explain the concept of the "bid-ask spread" to a frustrated beginner who wants to know why their account shows a slight loss the exact second they purchase a stock?
questions.q15: Retail trading volume naturally drops during prolonged "bear markets" (downtrends). How do we maintain user engagement and provide value on the platform when people are generally afraid to invest?
questions.q16: Write a program that accepts a user's age and a boolean indicating if they have a VIP pass. Use if/else if/else logic to determine their entry fee: Under 18 is $10, 18-64 is $20, 65+ is $15. If they have a VIP pass, apply a 50% discount to their final price after the age check.
questions.q17: Declare an array of 7 floating-point numbers representing the daily temperatures for a week. Write a loop to iterate through the array and calculate three things: the maximum temperature, the minimum temperature, and the average temperature for the week.
questions.q18: Write a program that accepts an integer representing the height of a pyramid. Use nested for loops to print a symmetrical pyramid made of asterisks (*) to the console. The outer loop should handle the rows, while the inner loops handle the spaces and the asterisks.
questions.q19: Create an abstract Product class (Abstraction) with a private stockLevel variable (Encapsulation). Create subclasses PhysicalProduct and DigitalProduct (Inheritance). Both must implement a calculateShipping() method, but DigitalProduct should override this to always return $0.00 (Polymorphism).
questions.q20: Create an abstract Character class with private health stats accessed only via specific getter methods. Create Mage and Warrior subclasses. Define a common attack() method in the base class, but override it so the Mage casts a spell (calculating magic damage) and the Warrior swings a sword (calculating physical damage).
questions.q21: Please record and upload a short video (approximately 1 minute) introducing yourself. Explain why we should offer you this internship and why you believe you are the right fit for this position. You must present entirely in English.
questions.q22: Please record and upload a split-screen video explaining your Final Project submission: why you chose to build this specific project over other options, what its practical use is, and how you went about developing it. The video must be split-screen, with one side showing a live walkthrough of your project and the other side showing your face as you speak. You must present entirely in English.
